subject: Urgent: FinBridge spike — request for incident logs and chain-of-custody
messages:
From: Arjun Patel <arjun@finbridge.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: FinBridge Ops <ops@finbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 14:03:12 -0700
Subject: Spike in error rate and latency - logs request

Monica —

We observed a severe spike with Redwood endpoints serving our production workload between ~19:45-20:30 UTC (local times above).
Symptoms: 5xx error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6.8%, tail latency (p99) increased from ~320ms to >1.8s, and overall throughput dropped by ~35%. This impacted 3 customer-facing pipelines.

Can you provide the incident logs and any KV cache dumps / runtime traces for that window? Specifically we need:
- Inference service access logs (request_id, model, route, latency, status) 19:30–21:00 UTC
- Runtime error traces for the failed requests
- Any autoscaling/eviction events and GPU telemetry that coincide with the window
- KV cache snapshots (if available) or indicators of cache thrashing

Also: we need a short written statement describing Redwood’s chain-of-custody for logs during an incident (who has access, how copies are created and stored, retention policy for incident artifacts). Our internal security team and our CTO are asking for this; they want exec-level confirmation since this is now an executive-facing incident.

This is high priority for FinBridge — please mark for exec attention and let us know ETA for artifacts.

Thanks,
Arjun
Ops Lead — FinBridge

---
Attachment: none
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Arjun Patel <arjun@finbridge.com>
Cc: FinBridge Ops <ops@finbridge.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:10:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in error rate and latency - logs request

Arjun —

Thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We’ve flagged this P1 internally and I’ve looped in Security for chain-of-custody & evidence packaging. Immediate next steps from our side: 

1) We will collect and stage an incident bundle covering 19:00–21:30 UTC including: request logs, runtime error traces, autoscaling events, GPU telemetry, and KV cache metadata.
2) We will provide a hash-signed archive and a short statement on our retention/chain-of-custody practices.
3) For sensitive content: we will remove direct customer PII by default and include an index of any redacted fields.

ETA: preliminary bundle available within 24 hours; full artifact package and executive summary within 48 hours.

To transfer artifacts securely, please confirm the upload method you prefer — we can:
- Place a presigned, access-logged S3 bundle (recommended)
- Grant temporary access to our secure evidence portal (requires corporate SSO)

I’m attaching an initial incident summary (incident_summary_v0.pdf) that is safe to circulate to your SOC team.

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident_summary_v0.pdf (stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:00:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in error rate and latency - logs request (security checklist)

Monica, Sean —

I’m on this. A couple of security/process notes before we hand over aggregated artifacts to FinBridge: 

- We should produce a formal evidence package (signed manifest, SHA256 hashes for each artifact, access log export describing who pulled what and when).
- Redact or pseudonymize any direct end-user identifiers unless FinBridge requires them and we have a signed justification.
- Confirm retention window requested by FinBridge. Our default incident artifact retention is 90 days unless the customer asks otherwise and signs a DPA addendum.
- We need to confirm whether FinBridge wants full request bodies. If so, route through Legal for a DPA amendment and get DocuSign sign-off.
- Prepare a chain-of-custody statement: who exported artifacts, approval stamps, storage location, and KMS key IDs used to encrypt the bundle.

Action items for SEs (Monica): collect the logs, compute hashes, and prepare the manifest. I’ll prepare a short security cover memo and coordinate with Legal if DocuSign is needed.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Team —

Draft for exec/CSO briefing (short):
- Incident window: 2026-05-20 19:45–20:30 UTC. Root cause under investigation; preliminary signals point to transient autoscaler misconfiguration + KV cache contention on a specific shard.
- Customer impact: FinBridge reported p99 latency increase and increased 5xx rates affecting three pipelines.
- Actions taken: P1 declared; incident bundle shared with customer (presigned link); signed manifest and chain-of-custody prepared; Security & Legal looped for DPA amendment if customer requests raw bodies.
